title: Sleep disturbances in inpatients receiving psychosomatic treatment: prospective course documentation and exploratory evaluation of a sleep-related psychoeducation
summary:
Background: Sleep problems are very common among people receiving inpatient psychosomatic treatment for psychological and physical complaints. Poor sleep can worsen other symptoms and reduce treatment success. So far, there are few programmes in inpatient psychosomatic care that focus specifically on sleep.

Aim: First, we want to describe how sleep problems change during an inpatient stay. Second, we want to obtain first indications of whether a new group programme on sleep (psychoeducation) helps to improve sleep.

Method: Adults with marked sleep problems who are treated as inpatients for at least six weeks can take part. First, 70 patients who receive usual treatment without the new programme are surveyed. Afterwards, 70 patients who additionally attend four group sessions on sleep are surveyed. All participants complete questionnaires on sleep, mood, distress and quality of life on a tablet within the first days after admission and six weeks later. The change in sleep is then compared between the two groups.

interventions.name: Group 1 – Baseline cohort (historical control, n = 70): Patients treated on the psychosomatic inpatient ward before the sleep-related psychoeducation group is introduced receive standard inpatient treatment without additional sleep-related psychoeducation. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Inpatient admission to the Department of Psychosomatic Medicine and Psychotherapy, ACURA Kliniken Baden-Baden
- Clinically relevant insomnia symptoms (Insomnia Severity Index, ISI ≥ 10)
- Expected length of stay ≥ 6 weeks
- Sufficient command of the German language
- Capacity to consent and written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Acute psychosis or acute suicidality
- Severe substance dependence
- Lack of informed consent
- Expected length of stay < 6 weeks
- Insufficient command of the German language
